rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for someone's pretentious or artificial display, used nominally for the behaviour itself.

example.english: They are always putting on an affectation, pretending to know everything when they do not.
example.traditional: 佢成日扮嘢，明明唔識就扮到自己乜都識咁。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 baan6 je5 ming4 ming4 m4 sik1 zau6 baan6 dou3 zi6 gei2 mat1 dou1 sik1 gam3

rows.note: Use this for a repeated small physical gesture or behavioural mannerism, such as touching the face while speaking.

example.english: Their affectation of constantly touching their face when nervous is very noticeable.
example.traditional: 佢一緊張就不停摸面，呢啲小動作好明顯。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 gan2 zoeng1 zau6 bat1 ting4 mo2 min6 ni1 di1 siu2 dung6 zok3 hou2 ming4 hin2

rows.note: Use this when the mannerism is an unusual or eccentric personal habit rather than merely a physical gesture.

example.english: They have an affectation of arranging all the dishes before eating.
example.traditional: 佢有個怪癖，食飯之前一定要將啲菜逐樣排好。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jau5 go3 gwaai3 pik1 sik6 faan6 zi1 cin4 jat1 ding6 jiu3 zoeng1 di1 coi3 zuk6 joeng6 paai4 hou2
